On 2026-10-15 both files in OSF project kjmpe (Dataset_Fluor_ommo.txt, 1419 bytes; Dataset_Red_Chroma.txt, 8230 bytes) downloaded without logging in and open as clean tab-separated tables; Metacheck also judged both usable. The OSF record says the project is public and both files were uploaded on 2021-01-13 and never changed, so they were public when Cooper's coders looked. The coder's note that access had to be requested most likely refers to OSF's 'request access' button, which asks to join the project as a contributor and is not needed to download files.; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: COOPER_ERROR (Cooper et al.'s coding is wrong). The KNB metadata record knb.1404.1 points to data object knb.1403.1 (ROMA_raw data.xlsx). That object's access rule allows public reading and has not changed since 2017-09-07, and the KNB search index links the two records. On 2026-10-15 the file downloaded without logging in (213,166 bytes) from https://knb.ecoinformatics.org/knb/d1/mn/v2/object/knb.1403.1 and passes metacheck's usability test (1296 rows by 16 columns; sheets ROMA_sites, ROMA_habitats, Metadata). Two of KNB's own download routes are broken, which probably misled the coder: the 'download package' route returns only an error text file, and the old file link in the metadata view returns 404. The data file itself was downloadable all along, so Cooper's No is wrong.; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: METACHECK_BUG (a Metacheck bug or limitation). Dryad dataset dryad.nvx0k6dpd holds one archive, Rcode_DataMEE_Duranetal.zip, whose name says it holds the R code and data. Inside are GeoTIFF rasters (for example 02_Lancover_Alt_Boundary/Present_landcover_2000.tif and Projected_Landuse_maps_00_13/Crop_00_13.tif) and shapefiles (02_Lancover_Alt_Boundary/Off_Muni_State_shp/*.shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj). On 2026-10-15 these opened directly with R terra (a 9902 x 8153 land-cover raster) and sf (11 state polygons). Metacheck classifies the .tif files as 'materials' and, since the GIS fix (#488), the shapefile parts as data, but it has no reader for spatial formats, so none of them counts as usable data (rechecked 2026-10-17 against metacheck 0.3.3.11), although GeoTIFF and shapefile are open standard formats. The only file it counts as data, Off_Table S1_Harmonisation_IUCN_IBGE_Apr2020.xlsx, is a land-cover classification lookup table with long text descriptions, which it correctly judges not usable.; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: METACHECK_BUG (a Metacheck bug or limitation). Metacheck's delimiter detection tries only comma, semicolon, tab and pipe, so it reads each file as one text column and judges none usable.; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: METACHECK_BUG (a Metacheck bug or limitation). The Dryad data file StudySite_2018_19.csv (dryad.c2fqz61bj, 452 MB, CC0, with README.docx describing every column) downloaded on 2026-10-15 and opens as 1,662,978 rows by 37 named columns with R read.table, data.table::fread and Python's csv.Sniffer. Metacheck never downloaded it (file_location empty) because data_check skips any single file above its 100 MB max_file_size limit. Even if downloaded it would fail: the file is space-separated despite the .csv extension, and metacheck's .sniff_delimiter() only tries comma, semicolon, tab and pipe, so data_read_head() reads it as one text column. The 22 OF_subtitles_*.txt files that Metacheck did open (folder misc/subtitles of the OpenFeeder software on GitHub and Zenodo) are firmware event-code lists, not data.; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: NOT_FAIR (the data, code or README were not shared in a FAIR way). It has a two-row header (section labels above the variable names) and its effect sizes are stored as text such as '0.94±0.0921' (mean ± SE), so the values cannot be used as numbers. Metacheck's 'not usable' is a correct reading of how the data were shared, not a parsing bug. Both sheets (Volatiles, Non-volatiles) are formatted publication tables: a two-row header with species names in the second row, group heading rows such as 'Esters', and every value stored as text in the form '0.220±0.126' (mean ± SE). Metacheck reads all 18 columns as text, so it judges the file not usable ('100% of columns are free text'). This is a correct reading of how the data were shared, not a parsing error. The file holds summary statistics written as text rather than machine-readable values, so Cooper is right that it downloads and opens, and Metacheck is right that it is not a usable dataset. Author's decision 2026-10-17: a formatted publication table is not FAIR data, so Metacheck's 'not usable as data' is right (METACHECK_RIGHT).; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: NOT_FAIR (the data, code or README were not shared in a FAIR way). The 15 files Data_bottlenose_S0-S4.dat, Data_pilot_S0-S4.dat and Data_Rissos_S0-S4.dat sit at the root of Dryad dataset dryad.wwpzgmsk4, which has no folders. Their names start with 'Data_' and Readme.txt lists them under 'Data:', so they are labelled as data. Each file is a model-input file for the Stan models: a '#name' line followed by a space-separated vector, with vectors of different lengths (142 yearly catches under #Catch, 32 survey years under #Y, 4 abundance estimates under #N). There is no row-and-column structure, so metacheck's reader gets one text column. Cooper's own data_open is 'Needs specific software or too large', so Cooper agrees that the files do not open as usable tables. The linked Zenodo records hold only Stan/R code (zenodo.4899113) and posterior summaries FullTable.MXSX.csv (zenodo.4899115), which are model output and not the raw data.; REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (third review: the actual repository files were listed and opened): CAUSE: UNSUPPORTED_FAIR_PLATFORM (a FAIR repository on a platform Metacheck does not support). The sequence data are in NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA717381: the European mirror lists 368 public runs (public since 2021-03-29), and SRR14074749_1.fastq.gz downloaded on 2026-10-15 and opens as a normal FASTQ file. Metacheck does not check NCBI SRA, so it found no repository for the paper's own data. The only repository it found, github.com/yhwu/idemp, is a third-party demultiplexing tool whose example files (barcode_sample.txt, I1/R1/R2.fastq) are not this paper's data.
